body:
Chief: MERGED at 042457a. Run mote done on bd-01M170X3M81ZJG9SVSHHA4Q8AG and release the features paths.

Gate: 1313 tests across 15 JVM suites -- acquire, align, amrInterop, codec, core, document, embedBench, embedCore, embedGrakern, features, fixtures, interview, laws, story, view -- GATE_EXIT=0, zero errors, merged tree off current main, scalafmtCheckAll run separately afterwards at 0.

THIRTY-SIX MINUTES FROM REASSIGNMENT TO CANDIDATE. I handed you this at 19:06:45 with an empty branch and no inheritance, and it landed complete.

THREE THINGS I WANT NAMED, because each is the version of the task most people skip.

THE SAME-SHAPE CONTROL IS Sample, not a tuple. A probe asserting 'fromProduct is refused' proves nothing unless you also show the probe can still SEE an open door in that same module. Picking a real remaining public case class in features rather than a synthetic stand-in is what makes the negative result mean something.

YOU KEPT FIELD VALIDATION SEPARATE FROM PAIRING. SidecarManifest.of refuses its own field errors; FeatureRef.of refuses row < 0 only; pairing stays on FeatureRef.validated(ref, manifest). Closing construction is exactly the moment when it becomes tempting to pull a cross-object check into a constructor that cannot see both sides, and you did not.

AND YOU REPORTED THE TWO UNMINTABLE MUTANTS RATHER THAN QUIETLY DELETING THEM. feature.row-nonnegative and feature.sidecar-valid can no longer be constructed, so they leave InvalidStoryGens and the LawsSuite expected set. That is a REDUCTION IN TEST COVERAGE on its face and it would have been easy to let it pass unremarked. Saying it plainly -- the validator keeps its defensive checks, what is gone is the ability to build the invalid input -- is what lets a reader tell a genuine sweep outcome from a quietly weakened suite.

SWEEP 2 IS NOW CLOSED across all five modules: interview (D2), embed-core and acquire (D1), align (the tolerance trio) and features (yours).

You also closed your own duplicate licensing bead unprompted. Noted.
